title: I’ve used the Pixel 11 Pro XL and iPhone 18 Pro Max, and Apple’s ecosystem isn’t enough anymore
summary: Pixels have closed the gap.
body: Comparing the latest iPhone and Pixel devices used to be troublesome. It always boiled down to the same thing. Either you were firmly entrenched in the iOS ecosystem and were stuck with Apple, or you’d never use an iPhone, no matter how many advantages it had. Two distinct camps existed, with little hope of much crossover. It was rare for a buyer to sit down and decide between the two, but times have changed. Google worked to make Pixels a more attractive alternative to the iPhone, from a sleeker design to more intuitive software, and the results have been positive. Meanwhile, Apple’s definitely come back to the pack, and what used to be an easy choice is anything but. I’ve used the iPhone 18 Pro Max and Pixel 11 Pro XL , and Apple’s ecosystem doesn’t have the hold it once did.

title: What if the next AI breakthrough isn’t a better chatbot?
summary: GPT learns through language, but JEPA learns from the world. What does this mean for next-gen API?
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority Love it or hate it, AI is increasingly good at helping write your emails, summarise a 100-page report, explain quantum physics, and generate a convincing image of just about anything. Give a modern AI model the right tools , and it can tackle complex, multi-step tasks, write code, and even build a small app or game with surprisingly little input. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini , and their competitors showcase increasingly impressive reasoning and agentic capabilities. But you’ve probably noticed some limitations, too. Sycophantic responses, overly verbose or formulaic prose, and difficulty grappling with the subtleties of complex problems remain familiar frustrations. It’s far from perfect. And while AI can be remarkably capable inside a computer, getting it to reliably do things in the physical world is a different challenge altogether.

title: Google Chat’s latest feature could finally end the post-meeting confusion
summary: Your meeting's biggest takeaways now land right where your team chats.
body: TL;DR Google Chat is getting automatic AI-powered meeting recaps that summarize discussions, decisions, and assigned action items. Recaps appear directly in meeting chats, complete with links to Gemini notes, recordings, and transcripts, so participants can catch up without digging through files. The feature is rolling out gradually to eligible Google Workspace subscribers. There’s always that one meeting where everyone agrees on the next steps, only for half the team to forget who promised what by lunchtime. Then comes the frantic search through notes, recordings, and chat messages to piece everything together. Google wants to put an end to that familiar office headache with a new Google Chat feature that brings the important stuff straight into your conversations after a meeting. In a blog post , Google revealed that Chat will automatically post meeting recaps once a Google Meet call ends. The feature builds on Meet’s Gemini-powered “ Take notes for me ” tool, turning its AI-generated notes into a handy summary that everyone in the meeting conversation can reference.

title: Google Sheets on iPhone finally catches up to Android with this Gemini upgrade
summary: Spreadsheets on your iPhone just got a brain.
body: TL;DR Google is bringing Gemini to Google Sheets on iPhones, following its rollout on the web and Android. You can ask Gemini questions about your spreadsheets, generate summaries, identify trends, and create charts. The feature is rolling out to eligible Google Workspace and Google AI subscribers and could take up to 15 days to reach everyone. Working with spreadsheets on a phone can be a pain, especially with hundreds of rows and columns. Google wants to make that experience less frustrating, and it’s now bringing Gemini to Google Sheets on iPhones. It is already available in Google Sheets on the web and, more recently, on Android . With its arrival on iOS , you can now ask Gemini questions about your spreadsheets, get quick summaries, and even create charts without pulling out your laptop. For example, say you’re looking at a spreadsheet tracking your monthly expenses. Instead of reviewing every transaction yourself, you can ask Gemini where you’ve spent the most. Similarly, if you’re reviewing a report, you can ask it to highlight important trends or turn the numbers into a chart that’s easier to understand.

title: After a few days with the Fitbit Edge, I think Google found the sweet spot
summary: Right in the middle.
body: 2026 has proven to be a really strong year for Google wearables. The $100 Fitbit Air is an excellent entry point into Google Health and a solid all-around fitness tracker for someone who doesn’t want the distractions and bulk of a smartwatch. For folks who do want a smartwatch, the Pixel Watch 5 is one of the best you can buy. But with a $399 starting price, it’s a lot more expensive, too. That’s what makes the new Fitbit Edge so compelling. At $180, it’s substantially cheaper than the Pixel Watch while still offering an interactive AMOLED display — something the Air lacks. But with fewer onboard apps, no speaker or microphone, and a really compact/lightweight design, it’s more approachable for people who don’t want the smartwatch life, but still want to check the time or see workout data on their wrist.

title: Swae Lee Announces 2027 Australian Same Difference Tour
summary: The rapper and singer will play five East Coast and West Coast dates in January, supporting his debut solo album.
body: Swae Lee is heading back to Australia. The rapper and singer has announced a five-date national tour for January 2027 in support of his debut solo album, Same Difference . The Australian run opens Jan. 6 at Melbourne’s Forum before heading to Sydney’s Enmore Theatre on Jan. 8 and Brisbane’s Fortitude Music Hall on Jan. 10. Shows at Adelaide’s Hindley Street Music Hall and Perth’s Metro City follow on Jan. 12 and Jan. 13, respectively. An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan Explanation: This is an unusual rainbow. For one thing, the rainbow is not complete, appearing only in a sunlit fan — but that by itself is not very unusual. What is most unusual is the fake location of the Sun . The Sun appears to be toward the front, just below those hills — but it is not. That is not how rainbows work . Rainbows involve a backward reflection from falling rain , so that the Sun must really be behind you . In this case, gaps between clouds near the setting Sun allowed rays to cross the entire sky and appear to converge in front , an unusual phenomenon called anticrepuscular rays . The photo was taken with a phone last week at sunset in Presenzano , Italy . The seemingly reverse rainbow was noticed when hanging up laundry .
